title: The sandpile

data.source: Bak-Tang-Wiesenfeld sandpile on a 40 x 40 table with open edges, random grain drops, seeded

prediction: If the whole pile is one count running to one threshold, big avalanches come at regular gaps (CV below 0.7) and a longer build-up gives a bigger slide (rank correlation above 0.2).
baseline: Self-organised criticality: a power law of sizes with no typical scale, big avalanches arriving almost at random (gap CV near 1), size not predictable from the wait.
why: Big avalanches come at gaps only a little steadier than chance, and a longer wait does not bring a bigger slide. The pile as a whole has no single count running to a threshold. Only each small square does, and that is the model's own definition.
